TastyBites Holdings - Q3 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the TastyBites Holdings Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during listen-only segments. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (VP, Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss TastyBites Holdings' Q3 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Growth Officer; and Marcus Hale, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on five key areas: performance in key channels including retail, foodservice, and convenience; updates on M&A activity and portfolio management; market share trends for major brands; performance of key brands and product categories; and organic revenue growth overall and by region.

First, regarding performance in key channels: retail, foodservice, and convenience. Our three core channels drove 8.2% year-over-year organic revenue growth, surpassing the broader Food & Beverage category's 4.1% IRI-measured growth. This strength comes from our emphasis on premiumization, snacking megatrends, and targeted distribution gains, even as input costs rose 6% sequentially on cocoa and edible oils.

In retail, our largest channel at 58% of total net revenues, we achieved 9.5% organic growth—our best in two years. Volume increased 4.2%, accelerating from Q2's 2.8%, thanks to double-digit gains in health-oriented products. CrunchyNut protein bars, now with 15 grams of plant-based protein per bar, saw dollar sales up 22% per IRI, grabbing 1.2 share points in the $12 billion U.S. nutrition bar segment, ahead of Clif and Kind. Pricing added 5.3%, in line with category norms, passing through 70% of commodity inflation with elasticity at -2.1, close to our -2.4 long-term target. ACV distribution rose 3.1 points to 92% nationally, with expanded shelf space at Walmart for ZestEnergy RTD beverages up 15%, Kroger savory snacks up 8%, and Albertsons. Velocity on TastyTwist tortilla chips improved 7% via demos and planograms. North America grew 11%, with e-commerce at 18% of retail sales—up from 12% YoY—through Amazon and Instacart bundles boosting basket rings 25%. EMEA hit 6% by pushing zero-sugar beverages to 35% of SKUs amid UK taxes. APAC managed 4% despite China's challenges, via mango-chili nuts with Reliance Retail. We're committing $50 million in FY23 to AI-driven assortment planning with IRI's Liquid Data for 2-3 more share points in functional snacks, outperforming Kellogg's 3% growth.

Foodservice, 25% of revenues, surged 12.8% organically, our top performer, as U.S. traffic hit 95% of 2019 levels per NPD. Volume rose 7.1%, beating channel growth of 3.5%, with operators favoring value menus amid 8% price inflation. McDonald's Spicy Blaze sauce rollout added $45 million, Starbucks NitroFuel energy shots hit 4,000 doors with 25% impulse lift via BIB. Casual dining like Chili's and Applebee's saw 15% appetizer check ups from premium nachos. Pricing contributed 5.7%, mix shifting to 20% protein dips. U.S. led at 15%, LatAm 9% with USD contracts despite Argentina inflation, Europe 5% countered by 40% recycled packaging. Our $30 million innovation fund supports DoorDash ghost kitchens with 20% higher margins on spice blends. This channel's 22% EBITDA margin beats retail's 18%, unlike Hershey's retail focus.

Convenience, 17% of revenues, grew 7.9% organically, topping NACS's 5.2%. Volume up 3.8% with c-store traffic up 4%, shining in $28 billion impulse. 7-Eleven ThunderBolt energy drinks gained 2.5 share points and 28% volume via displays. Wawa and Sheetz GrabNGo nuts up 12% velocity. Beverages grew 15% vs. Red Bull's 11% with 16-ounce shareables. Pricing at 4.1% with less promo. U.S. Southeast +10% via Circle K, APAC 8% with 7-Eleven Japan seltzers, Canada 4% via stevia reformulation. VSA to 5,000 doors, RFID cut OOS 30%, compostable wrappers meet CSP goals. Margins at 24% from KeHE and Core-Mark efficiency.

Overall, mix shifted 100 basis points to higher-margin foodservice and convenience, lifting gross margins to 38.2%, 200 basis points above guidance. Trends like snacking fatigue and 12% CAGR premium RTD per Euromonitor favor our 45% better-for-you portfolio. Q4 growth eyed at 7-9%, $100 million SAP S/4HANA savings funding innovation, 80% hedging through H1'24 despite FX and palm oil risks.

Second, concerning updates on M&A activity and portfolio management. These remain key to sustainable high-margin growth in health & wellness beverages, plant-based snacks, and premium convenience, divesting low-return assets. Our core portfolio's adjusted EBITDA CAGR is 8% over three years, beating industry 4-5% per NielsenIQ and IRI.

In Q2, we acquired VitalRoots Nutritionals for $450 million cash, adding $180 million revenue RTD protein shakes and adaptogen waters at 22% EBITDA—above our 18% beverages average. This taps $12 billion U.S. functional market at 12% CAGR on wellness trends. Synergies hit $15 million run-rate cost savings via Midwest aseptic filling, cutting third-party costs 25%; $20 million revenue from cross-selling at Walmart and Kroger. Expect 150 bps EPS accretion FY24, ROIC over 15% by year three.

In Q3, divested Heritage Confections including SweetBite for $320 million to PE, $250 million revenue at 8% EBITDA and 1-2% growth amid -3% U.S. candy decline per Circana. Proceeds $280 million net for repurchases and debt, net leverage to 2.1x. Cuts 5% low-growth revenues, adds 80 bps margins.

Internationally, EuroSnack Innovations in Germany for €220 million ($240 million), €95 million sales at 15% organic on clean-label (68% EU consumer priority per Kantar), boosting EMEA savory snacks share to 12%, COGS down 12% on pea protein. APAC: $180 million for Thai FreshWave Juices stake, $60 million at 18% growth like Olipop, joint R&D for halal low-sugar to Indonesia/Philippines.

North America M&A drives 6% organic in health beverages vs. 4% category. LatAm organic 9% in convenience, eyeing plant-based dairy at 14% CAGR Mexico. Hedged 70% FY24 volumes amid cocoa +150% YTD, diversified shea.

We've shed $1.2 billion underperformers since 2021 (15% portfolio), lifting organic to 5.2%, margins 19.5%. Power brands like ZeroSugar Cola +11%, NutriCrunch chips +2 share now 75% revenues at 10%+ growth. $250 million annual R&D on fermentation, AI flavors; five functional SKUs Q4 for $50 billion wellness.

Pipeline $2-3 billion next 18 months, >20% margins/10% growth, funded by $1.5 billion FCF, 4% capex. Themes: regenerative ag for Scope 3, blockchain traceability cutting recalls 30%.

These position us for 7-9% revenue growth, 200-250 bps margin expansion FY24, ROIC >12%.

Third, in terms of market share trends for major brands. Across CSDs, energy, functionals, RTD teas per Nielsen/IRI ACV and velocity, we hold 18.4% U.S. non-alc share in $120 billion retail, +110 bps YoY, +240 bps two-year, strongest since 2019. 4.2% ACV gain in c-stores/e-comm vs. category -1.1%.

CSDs $45 billion: AquaFizz 22.7% volume flat but +1.8% dollar on zero-sugar now 35% mix (from 22%), vs. Coke 43.2% (-80 bps), Pepsi 28.1%. 15% R&D stevia lift 12% penetration per Circana.

Energy $14 billion +8.7%: MaxEnergy 26.4% (+320 bps) over Monster 24.8% (-150 bps), Red Bull 31.2% (-2.1) via Energy+ Wellness 42% trial share. Amazon bundles to 32% online ACV, March Madness 5x ROAS.

Functionals/RTD teas $22 billion +6.2%: BevMax 14.9% (+2.4) on probiotic teas +18% mass, vs. Bubly 16.7%, Snapple 11.3%. Biotech probiotic repeat 28% vs. 19%.

North America (75% revenue): U.S. gains offset Canada LCBO; Mexico CSD 19.2% (-0.5) offset RTD. EMEA (15%) +1.7 to 12.8% on UK zero-sugar/HFSS, Germany energy +22% Euro 2024. APAC (8%) +4.1 to 9.6% China e-comm kombucha, India 7.2% pilot JioMart +30% MoM. LATAM (2%) 8.1%, Brazil energy +15% soccer.

Health-Premium-Growth: Divested $250 million legacy, 12 launches like collagen shots, 100% recycled PET 2025 lifts Europe equity 8 points YouGov. FY24 +150-200 bps share, $400 million digital AI forecasting -25% stockouts, $1.2 billion plant-based tuck-in. Buffer 42% gross vs. FX/SNAP risks.

Fourth, looking at performance of key brands and product categories. These drove 8.2% net sales to $2.52 billion, organic +6.1% ex-FX/acquisitions, on resilient demand, premiumization, innovation in health/wellness/plant-based.

Beverages 42% sales +10.5% YoY, organic +8.2%: VitaBoost Energy +15% to $450 million, +2.2 share U.S. energy per Nielsen on Zero Sugar stevia/electrolytes -40% sugar, ACV 92%. North America 12%, EMEA 14% to 11.5% share vs. Red Bull, APAC 5% offset e-comm Tmall/Shopee 22% mix. PureHarvest juices +9% cold-pressed +4% price, Florida membrane filtration +12% yield -25% water, margins 32.4% +110 bps.

Snacks 28% +7.8%, organic +6.4%: NutriCrunch veggie chips +18% $320 million +3.1 share healthy aisle 9% CAGR IRI, TikTok Gen Z +14% penetration. EliteHarvest nuts +11% almond $2.45/lb forwards. Potato chips -2% private label, delist 15 SKUs to 8.2x turns. LATAM 11% NutriCrunch FEMSA OXXO, EMEA 5% volume recyclable 85% pouches. Margins 28.7% +90 bps John Deere ag -18% waste.

Dairy/alts 18% +9.1%, organic +7.3%: GreenMeadow plant yogurts +22% $280 million oat/almond Probiotic Power 95 IRI 4.5x repeat +1.8 share vs. Chobani/Danone. CheddarPeak +4% foodservice +13% McD. Precision fermentation Perfect Day -50% carbon FY26 EU Green. APAC 15% Indonesia, North America 8%. Margins 30.2% +140 bps Wisconsin ultrasonic.

Convenience 12% +5.2%, organic +4.1%: QuickBite bowls +16% $150 million $25B frozen high-protein low-carb GLP-1. APAC flat rice offset HelloFresh. $50M HPP +30% shelf no preservatives.

Premium 45% sales (from 38%) 2x margins. Scope 3 -12% regen ag, 65% recyclable. APAC capex 30% $400M FY24 tariff hedge. Q3 organic 6-8% led VitaBoost/GreenMeadow. 12% R&D vs. 4% industry, fermented bolt-on vs. corn $4.80.

Finally, reviewing organic revenue growth: overall and by region. Organic growth was 5.2% YoY constant currency, ex-GreenMoo acquisition and 1.8 points FX tailwinds—sixth straight positive quarter, up from 3.9% Q3 2022 amid Ukraine/avian disruptions.

Decomp: Pricing +3.9 points vs. 4.2% COGS inflation oils/corn easing; mix +1.1 premium like VitaGlow bars/low-sugar RTD +12% vs. value +8 points gap; volume +0.2 on QSR/c-store traffic, Nielsen +1.5% salty penetration like Pepsi Frito-Lay.

North America 48% revenues +7.1%: Pricing +4.8 EDLP VitaCrunch +110 bps $25B savory vs. Pringles; volume/mix +2.3 VitaBurger patties $45M Beyond-like pea QSR Burger King Canada. E-comm +28% Amazon/Instacart club soft.

EMEA 28% +4.8%: Pricing +3.2 Euro 7% CPI Germany, volume flat AI NielsenIQ trade -15%; mix +1.6 PureSip collagen +18% UK/Nordics €12B health. Palm labeling France reroute 20% cocoa Ivory Coast.

APAC 16% +3.5% from Q2 1.2: Volume +1.4 China, pricing +2.1 selective Indonesia. ZenLeaf RTD tea +22% India/SE matcha/kombucha $8B Euromonitor. Dragonfly micro-fulfillment China OOS 2% from 8% vs. Uni-President.

LATAM 8% +6.9%: Pricing +2.7 vs. 10% inflation, volume/mix +4.2 FestaFiesta lime-chili +150 bps $15B impulse OXXO/Femsa FIFA. Divest $120M sugar to alt-milk Danone-like $2B.

FY24 4-6% organic: R&D $250M Singapore upcycled hedge wheat $7.50 70%; Planogram 2.0 500k doors +3-5% velocity; 1,200 SKU delist Mondelēz-like. Dairy -5% QoQ to EBIT 14.5% +50-75 bps.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3. Net sales were $2.52 billion, representing an 8.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.2%, impacted positively by channel mix shift and productivity gains. Operating income was $480 million, and earnings per share were $1.45. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.4 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for net sales growth of 7-9%, adjusted EBITDA margins expanding 200 basis points, and EPS of $5.80 to $6.00.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

Emily Carter (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thanks, Emily. Inflation remains a headwind, with input costs up 6% sequentially on cocoa and edible oils, and broader COGS at 4.2%. We've passed through 70% via targeted pricing—3.9 points overall organic contribution—holding elasticity near targets at -2.1. Mix shifts to premium helped, and hedging 70-80% volumes through H1'24, plus diversified sourcing like West African shea and forward contracts on almonds, corn at $4.80/bushel, wheat $7.50, shields us. Productivity from SAP, AI planning, and tech like membrane filtration, HPP, ultrasonic cuts waste/yield boosts add buffer. Our 38.2% gross gives resilience vs. peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Raj Patel (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for new products and what is the expected impact?

Taylor Kim (Chief Growth Officer):
Great question, Raj. Our pipeline has 17 new SKUs this year, five functional snacks Q4 targeting $50 billion wellness. Standouts like VitaBoost Zero Sugar relaunch -40% sugar +electrolytes, +15% sales +2.2 share; GreenMeadow Probiotic plant yogurts +22% 4.5x repeat; QuickBite GLP-1 bowls +16%; VitaBurger patties $45M run-rate. 12% R&D spend accelerates precision fermentation, upcycled, AI flavors. Expect 150-200 bps share gains FY24, premium mix to 45% driving 2x margins, velocity +3-5% from Planogram Optimizer across 500k doors.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Laura Chen (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Marcus Hale (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Thanks, Laura. Disruptions from Ukraine, avian, China COVID easing, but we rerouted 20% cocoa, locked 70% FY24 volumes USD contracts LatAm, regen ag Scope 3 -12%, John Deere precision -18% potato waste. RFID convenience OOS -30%, Dragonfly China micro-fulfillment OOS 2%, Midwest aseptic VitalRoots -25% costs, SAP S/4HANA $100M savings. Blockchain traceability -30% recall risk, diversified West Africa shea palm volatility. Hits 40% recycled EU, 65-85-100% packaging goals. Resilient for 7-9% Q4 channel growth.

Operator:
Our last question comes from David Wong with Barclays. Please proceed.

David Wong (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Jordan Lee (CFO):
David, thanks. FY24 reaffirmed: 7-9% revenue, organic 4-6% sustained, margins +200-250 bps to 19.5-20%, EPS $5.80-6.00, ROIC >12%. Q4 channels 7-9%, categories 6-8% led VitaBoost/GreenMeadow. $1.5B FCF funds $2-3B M&A pipeline adjacencies >20% EBITDA/10% growth, 4% capex APAC tilt. Moderating costs dairy -5% QoQ, productivity funds innovation. Risks FX APAC, SNAP, commodities hedged; strengths premium 45%, share +150-200 bps, digital -25% stockouts.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in TastyBites Holdings. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
